fields.description:
## Problem
Once the review-kernel's downstream consumers no longer read `severity` (sibling tickets 1-5),
the review-kernel (`pass3_decide`) itself should stop STAMPING `severity` onto its own emitted
findings, since it is the one remaining source of the impact-only label this epic retires.

CORRECTED SCOPE (post-decomposition research): `findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES` vocabulary,
`normalize_finding`'s severity clamp, and the `Finding` Pydantic field are NOT removed --
research established they serve a completion-verification module cluster
(`completion_reconcile.py`, `completion_child_gate.py`, `epic_bug_screen.py`,
`workflow/gate_ops.py`, `workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py`) that hardcodes `severity`
as its ONLY signal (no `priority`/`decision`/`impact`/`validity` anywhere in that call path),
and `spec_scan.py`'s independent LLM reviewer. Deleting that shared machinery would break both
with no fallback and is out of scope for this epic entirely. Similarly,
`completion_verdict.schema.json`'s findings NEVER come from the review-kernel (always from the
completion-verification cluster), so its `severity` requirement is unaffected and stays
required. Only `review_result.schema.json` (populated by `shim.py`, which mixes
review-kernel-sourced findings with, potentially, others) needs `severity` relaxed from
required to optional, since a review-kernel-sourced finding will no longer carry it.

## Approach
1. Remove the `sev = severity_label(imp)` stamp from `pass3_decide`'s emitted finding dict
   (`review_kernel/decide.py`) at all of its return sites -- keep `severity_label()` itself as
   an internal impact-bucketing helper (still used by calibration/eval code and
   `test_divergence_grade_split.py`), just stop writing its output into the finding.
2. In `code_review/shim.py::_to_common_finding`, stop defaulting an absent `severity` to
   `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT = "medium"` -- when the source kernel finding has no `severity` (now the
   normal case for review-kernel findings), omit the `severity` key from the output entirely
   rather than emitting a misleading default. Delete `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` and
   `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT` from `shim.py` (their only use site).
3. In `common.schema.json`'s `$defs/finding`, remove `severity` from the `required` list
   (leave the `severity` property and the `$defs/severity` enum definition in place -- other
   producers, e.g. `completion_verdict`'s findings, still always supply it).
4. Remove the vestigial `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES`/`blocking_severities` field and its
   env-var registration from `review_bot/config.py` (already unused in the current
   `code_review_decision` flow per `adapter.py`'s own docstring).
5. Add ONE compatibility-note entry to `docs/release-notes.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`: `severity`
   is no longer guaranteed present on review-kernel-sourced findings within `review_result`
   (the field is now optional on that schema, not removed); `completion_verdict` findings are
   unaffected and always carry it.
6. Amend `docs/adr/0108-retire-severity-label.md` with an "Amendment" section (matching the
   style of `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md`'s own amendment) recording this corrected,
   narrower scope: `findings.py`'s shared severity vocabulary is retained for non-kernel
   producers; only the review-kernel stops stamping it; the schema change is a relaxation
   (required -> optional) on `review_result` only, not a field deletion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `grep -n '"severity"' src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` finds no finding-shape
  stamping (the `severity_label` function definition and any historical comments are
  acceptable).
- [ ] `common.schema.json`'s `$defs/finding.required` no longer lists `severity`; the
  `severity` property and `$defs/severity` enum remain defined.
- [ ] `review_bot/config.py` has no `blocking_severities`/`DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES` symbol;
  `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` and `tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py` are updated to
  assert the symbol's absence.
- [ ] `grep -n "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY\|_SEVERITY_DEFAULT" src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py`
  returns no matches.
- [ ] `docs/release-notes.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `docs/adr/0108-retire-severity-label.md`
  (Amendment section) each record the corrected, narrower scope.
- [ ] `make test` passes with the full suite, including
  `pytest tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py -k test_severity_label_buckets` and
  `pytest tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py` (proving `severity_label()` itself is
  untouched) and the full `completion_reconcile`/`completion_child_gate`/`epic_bug_screen`
  test suites (proving the completion-verification cluster's own `severity` usage is
  unaffected).

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit tests (schema validation of a review-kernel finding dict with no
`severity` key passes `common.schema.json`'s relaxed finding validator) plus a contract test
(`pass3_decide`'s real output fed to the schema validator, and separately `shim.py`'s
translation of a severity-less kernel finding, confirmed to omit `severity` rather than
default it). Oracle: schema validation succeeds without `severity` on a review-kernel-sourced
finding; a `completion_verdict`-shaped finding continues to require and carry `severity`
unchanged (negative/contrast case proving the narrower scope). `severity_label()`'s own
existing tests (`test_severity_label_buckets`, `test_divergence_grade_split.py`) keep passing
unchanged, proving the helper's behavior is untouched even though it's decoupled from the
Finding shape.
